body_ar:
خصائص البنات

ما حكم اختتان البنات؟

الجواب: أن هذا هو الذي يسمى بالخفاض و هو مكرمة أي من الأمور التي فيها استحباب إذا احتيج إليه فإذا عرف أهل الخبرة الحاجة إلى ذلك كان مستحبا و إذا لم يروا حاجة لذلك لم يكن مستحبا فليس هو مثل الختان في حق الرجال.

------------------------------------------------------------

ذم السؤال عن كيفية اتصاف الله سبحانه وتعلى بصفاته

هل وصف الله تعالى بأنه على عرشه بذاته ومع الناس بعلمه وحفظه وصف له بالجهة والمكان والتجسيم؟

هذا السؤال صاحبه مخلط عليه ينبغي أن يتوب إلى الله تعالى من مثل هذا النوع من الشبه، وأن يعلم أن هذا النوع هو من اتباع المتشابه ولا يسأل عنه إلا من كان مفتونا قد أصيب بفتنة إما دبت إليه بسماعها من غيره أو وصلت إليه هو بسبب ذنب من الذنوب، فالله سبحانه وتعالى أخبر عن نفسه بالحق الذي لا يمكن أن يشك فيه مؤمن، وما أخبر به عن نفسه فهو الحق، سواء فهمناه أو لم نفهمه فهو الحق، ونحن نعلم أن الله تعالى يقول: {الرحمن على العرش استوى} ونعلم أن ما قاله الله حق، ولا نبحث عن كيفيات ذلك ولا عن هيآته،

وقد سئل مالك عن سؤال نظير هذا السؤال، سأله رجل فقال: كيف استوى، فقال: الاستواء معلوم، والكيف مجهول والإيمان به واجب والسؤال عنه بدعة وما أراك إلا صاحب سوء أخرجوه عني.

------------------------------------------------------------

ذم الغلو والتساهل في تعظيم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ما رأيكم فيمن يضلل العلماء ويكفرهم لأنهم لا يتغالون في تقديس رسول الله ؟

بالنسبة لظاهرة التكفير والتبديع والتفسيق مع الأسف لم ينج منها أحد حتى أهل الاعتدال والتوازن أصبح اعتدالهم وتوازنهم يقتضي منهم ضريبة يدفعونها وهي أنهم لم يرضوا طائفة من الطوائف الغالية، فهؤلاء الغلاة المتشددون يذمونهم بالتساهل، وأولئك المنحلون يذمونهم بالتشدد فدفعوا ضريبة توازنهم حين عاداهم الجميع، وهذا دليل على صدقهم وتوسطهم في الأمر،

ومن هنا فإن أهل الغلو سواء كان ذلك الغلو في شخص رسول الله (ص) الذي قال وهو الصادق المصدوق لا تطروني كما أطرت النصارى عيسى ابن مريم ولكن قولوا عبد الله ورسوله، وكان (ص) يكره هذا الإطراء وهذا الغلو فقد أتاه أعرابي فلما مثل بين يديه أخذته الرعدة فارتعشت فرائصه فقال له رسول الله (ص) هون عليك فإنني لست بملك إنما أنا عبد الله ورسوله، فرسول الله (ص) نهى عن هذه المظاهر وهي مخالفة لهديه ولما جاء به، ولا يمكن أن يتحبب إليه ولا أن يتقرب إليه بما يخالف ما جاء به عن ربه عز وجل،

لكن مع هذا أيضا لا بد أن ندرك جميعا أن مما يقتضي محبة رسول الله (ص) التي شرطها الله في كتابه أن ندرس سيرته وسنته وهديه، وأن نتعلق بشخصه (ص) وأن نحبه غاية المحبة فإنه شرط علينا في الإيمان أن يكون حبنا له أشد من حبنا لأنفسنا التي بين جوانحنا، قال لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه حين قال له: يا رسول الله! لأنت أحب إلي من كل شيء إلا من نفسي التي بين جنبي، فقال : لا حتى أكون أحب إليك من نفسك التي بين جنبيك، فقال: والله الذي لا إله غيره لأنت أحب إلي من نفسي التي بين جنبي، وكذلك في حديث أبي هريرة وأنس رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله (ص) قال: لا يؤمن أحدكم حتى أكون أحب إليه من والده وولده،

فلذلك لا بد أن نراجع حب رسول الله (ص) في قلوبنا دون غلو، فكثير من الناس يظن أن ترك الغلو يقتضي أيضا نقص محبة رسول الله (ص)، وهذا غلط وعدم اعتدال، لا بد أن يعتدل الإنسان ويحاول أن يزيد حبه لله ورسوله، ويزيد تعلقه برسول الله (ص) وسنته ومحبته غاية المحبة، ولا يقتضي به ذلك الخروج عما جاء به رسول الله (ص).

----------------------------------------------------------------

شبه المشعوذين

ما حكم من قال إن شيخه أتى شخصا تذرف عيناه وقال له إن ابني حضره الموت وقال الشيخ وبإزائه ابن له يا مولانا خذ ابني هذا مكانه يعني ولد الشخص الذي أتاه فوقع ابن الشيخ صريعا من حينه ومات من حينه و قام ابن ذالك الشخص وما به وجع و هو الآن حي و القصة متواترة أريد حكم من يعتقد هذا؟

هذا من التخريف البين ومن مخالفة الشرع الواضحة فشيخه هذا الذي يزعم قد عصى الله قطعا حين دعي على ولده بالموت وقد حرم عليه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذالك ونهاه عنه وحرم على الآباء والأمهات الدعاء على الأولاد وهو لا يملك عمر ابنه حتى يهبه لمن شاء والله سبحانه و تعالى هو الذي يحيي ويميت ومن انقضى أجله لا يمكن أن يأخر ساعة و لا أن يعجل قال الله تعالى: ﴿فإذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون﴾

ولو كان هذا الشيخ عاقلا لدعى الله أن يشفي المريض ولم يدع على الصحيح بل ربما يكون هذا كحال مسيلمة الكذاب الذي سمع أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بصق في بئر كانت ملحا فصارت عذبا فبصق هو في بئر كانت ملحا فيبست وسمع أنه مسح على رأس صبي كان أقرع فنبت شعره ولم يشب حتى مات فمسح هو على رأس صبي كان صحيحا فقرع فهذا النوع يسمى بالإهانة

وأيضا فإن زعم التواتر في مثل هذا الأمر باطل قطعا فالتواتر اصطلاح ومعناه إخبار عدد من الناس يستحيل توافقهم على الكذب عادة عن أمر محسوس يستوي طرفاه و وسطه في ذالك طرفاه أي البداية و النهاية فيه في الإسناد هذا هو التواتر وهذا لا يمكن أن يصح في مثل هذا النوع من القصص الخرافية.

----------------------------------------------------------------

مواقف الآخرة

من المعلوم أن أول وقفة من مواقف الآخرة هي القبر و هو إما روضة من رياض الجنة أو حفرة من حفر النار و ما دام الأمر ذلك فلما ذا يكون الفزع من المواقف الأخرى كتطاير الصحف و كالصراط إلى آخره؟

إن كل مشهد من مشاهد الآخرة ينسي ما قبله كل مشهد أيا كان ينسي ما سبقه فينسى الإنسان كلما شهد له به و كلما رأي حتى الإنسان في قبره إذا عرض عليه مقعده من الجنة ينسى ذلك عند البعث و في المحشر ينسى ذلك بالكلية و عند وزن الأعمال ينسى ذلك بالكلية و هكذا فكل موقف من المواقف ينسى الإنسان كل ما قبله

و لذلك فالقبر أعظم من كل ما قبله و أعظم منه كل ما بعده اللحظة الأولى التي يعيش فيها الإنسان تحت الأرض في قبره تقتضي تغيرا عجيبا لمفاهيمه و أموره فما نتصوره نحن الآن عن الموت و تصورنا لأهل القبور و حالهم تصور مغلوط خاطئ بالكلية و لهذا قال الله تعالى: ﴿و بدا لهم من الله مالم يكونوا يحتسبون﴾ و قال تعالى: ﴿و جاءت سكرة الموت بالحق ذلك ما كنت منه تحيد و نفخ في الصور ذلك يوم الوعيد و جاءت كل نفس معها سائق و شهيد لقد كنت في غفلة من هذا فكشفنا عنك غطاءك فبصرك اليوم حديد﴾

فيتجلى للإنسان كثير مما كان مختفيا عنه و لهذا فأول ما يلقاه الإنسان في قبره ضمة القبر التي تختلف منها الأضلاع و تزول منها الحمائل ثم بعدها سؤال الملكين ما ربك و ما دينك و ما كنت تقول في هذا الرجل ثم تتتالى مشاهد القبر بعد ذلك و الليلة الأولى التي يمكثها الإنسان بين الموتى و لم يعرفهم من قبل ليلة عظيمة و لذاك جاء في الحديث:«ليلتان لم تسمع الخلائق بمثلهما، ليلة يبيت مع الموتى و لم يبت معهم قبلها و ليلة صبيحتها يوم القيامة»
body_en:
Matters particular to girls

What is the ruling on the circumcision of girls?

The answer: this is what is called al-khifāḍ, and it is a mark of honour (makrumah) — that is, one of the matters in which there is recommendation where there is need for it. So if those with expert knowledge recognise a need for it, it is recommended (mustaḥabb); and if they do not see a need for it, it is not recommended. It is not like circumcision in the case of men.

--------------------------------------------------------------

Censure of asking about the manner in which God, glorified and exalted, is described by His attributes

Is describing God, exalted, as being upon His Throne in His essence, and with people by His knowledge and His preserving, a describing of Him with direction, place and corporeality?

The one who asks this question is confused. He should repent to God, exalted, of this kind of doubt, and should know that this kind of thing is following the ambiguous (mutashābih), and that no one asks about it except one who is afflicted, who has been struck by a trial — whether it crept upon him by hearing it from someone else, or reached him on account of some sin.

God, glorified and exalted, has told about Himself the truth, which no believer can doubt; and what He has told about Himself is the truth, whether we understand it or do not understand it — it is the truth. We know that God, exalted, says: {The Merciful rose over the Throne} (Sūrat Ṭāhā 20:5), and we know that what God has said is true; and we do not search out the manners of that, nor its forms.

Malik was asked a question like this question. A man asked him: 'How did He rise?' And he said: 'The rising is known, the manner is unknown, belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation. And I do not think you are anything but an evil man. Take him out of my presence.'

--------------------------------------------------------------

Censure of excess, and of laxity, in the veneration of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace

What is your view of one who declares scholars misguided and declares them unbelievers because they do not go to excess in sanctifying the Messenger of God?

As for the phenomenon of declaring people unbelievers, innovators and transgressors: regrettably, no one has escaped it, not even the people of moderation and balance. Their moderation and balance has come to exact from them a tax they must pay, namely that they have not satisfied any one of the factions of excess: these extremists, the hardliners, reproach them for laxity, and those lax ones reproach them for severity. So they have paid the tax of their balance in that everyone has become hostile to them — and that is evidence of their sincerity and of their holding to the middle in the matter.

From here, the people of excess — whether that excess concerns the person of the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, who said, and he is the truthful and trusted one: 'Do not extol me as the Christians extolled Jesus son of Mary, but say: the servant of God and His Messenger.' And he, upon whom be peace, disliked this extolling and this excess: a bedouin came to him, and when he stood before him trembling seized him and his limbs shook, so the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, said to him: 'Be at ease; I am not a king — I am only the servant of God and His Messenger.' So the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, forbade these displays, and they are contrary to his guidance and to what he brought. It is not possible to make oneself beloved to him, nor to draw near to him, by what contradicts what he brought from his Lord, mighty and majestic.

But along with this, we must all also realise that among the things which love of the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace — the love God made a condition in His Book — requires of us is that we study his biography, his sunnah and his guidance; that we attach ourselves to his person, upon whom be peace; and that we love him with the utmost love. For He has made it a condition upon us in faith that our love for him be stronger than our love for our own selves within our breasts. He said to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, when Umar said to him: 'O Messenger of God, you are dearer to me than everything except my own self that is between my two sides' — he said: 'No, not until I am dearer to you than your own self that is between your two sides.' So he said: 'By God, besides whom there is no god, you are dearer to me than my own self that is between my two sides.' Likewise in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and Anas, may God be pleased with them, that the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, said: 'None of you believes until I am dearer to him than his father and his child.'

For that reason we must examine the love of the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, in our hearts — without excess. Many people suppose that giving up excess also requires a diminishing of love for the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace; and this is a mistake and a want of balance. A person must be balanced, and must strive to increase his love for God and His Messenger, and to increase his attachment to the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, and to his sunnah, and his love of him to the utmost — and that must not lead him to depart from what the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, brought.

--------------------------------------------------------------

The specious claims of charlatans

What is the ruling on one who says that his shaykh was approached by a man whose eyes were streaming, who said to him 'my son is at the point of death'; and the shaykh — with a son of his own beside him — said, 'O our Master, take this son of mine in his place', meaning in place of the son of the man who had come to him; and the shaykh's son fell down dead on the spot and died on the spot, while that man's son got up with no pain in him and is alive today; and the story is mass-transmitted? I want the ruling on one who believes this.

This is manifest drivel, and plain opposition to the revealed law. This shaykh of his whom he claims certainly disobeyed God when he supplicated against his son for death; the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made that forbidden to him and prohibited it to him, and forbade fathers and mothers to supplicate against their children. He does not own his son's lifespan, that he might make a gift of it to whomever he wishes. God, glorified and exalted, is the One who gives life and causes death, and whoever's term has run out cannot be put back an hour, nor brought forward. God, exalted, said: {And when their term comes, they will not be put back an hour, nor will they be brought forward} (Sūrat al-Aʿrāf 7:34).

Had this shaykh been of sound mind, he would have supplicated to God to heal the sick one, and would not have supplicated against the healthy one. Rather, this may well be like the case of Musaylimah the Liar, who heard that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, spat into a well that was salt and it became sweet, so he spat into a well that was salt and it dried up; and heard that he wiped the head of a boy who was bald and his hair grew and he did not go grey until he died, so he wiped the head of a boy who was sound and the boy went bald. This kind is called humiliation.

Also, the claim of mass transmission in such a matter is certainly void. For mass transmission (tawātur) is a technical term, and its meaning is the report of a number of people whose agreement upon a lie is, in the customary course of things, impossible, concerning a matter perceived by the senses, with its two ends and its middle equal in that — its two ends, that is, the beginning and the end of it in the chain of transmission. This is mass transmission, and it cannot hold in this kind of fabulous story.

--------------------------------------------------------------

The stations of the Hereafter

It is known that the first station of the stations of the Hereafter is the grave, and that it is either a garden of the gardens of Paradise or a pit of the pits of the Fire. Since the matter is so, why is there terror at the other stations — such as the scattering of the scrolls, and the Bridge, and so on?

Every scene of the Hereafter makes one forget what is before it. Every scene, whatever it is, makes one forget what preceded it, so that a person forgets everything that was shown to him and everything he saw. Even the person in his grave, when his seat in the Garden is shown to him, forgets that at the resurrection; and at the gathering he forgets it entirely; and at the weighing of deeds he forgets it entirely; and so on. At every station a person forgets everything before it.

For that reason the grave is greater than everything before it, and everything after it is greater than the grave. The first moment in which a person lives beneath the earth in his grave brings about an astonishing change in his conceptions and his affairs. What we now imagine about death, and our imagining of the people of the graves and of their condition, is an entirely mistaken and erroneous imagining. That is why God, exalted, said: {And there will appear to them from God what they had not reckoned with} (Sūrat al-Zumar 39:47). And He, exalted, said: {And the agony of death comes with the truth: that is what you were trying to evade. And the Horn is blown: that is the Day of the Threat. And every soul comes, with it a driver and a witness. You were heedless of this, so We have removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp} (Sūrat Qāf 50:19–22).

So much that was hidden from a person becomes manifest to him. For this reason, the first thing a person meets in his grave is the squeezing of the grave, from which the ribs are displaced and the bearing-straps come apart; then after it the questioning of the two angels: who is your Lord, what is your religion, and what did you use to say about this man? Then the scenes of the grave follow one upon another after that.

And the first night that a person passes among the dead, not having known them before, is a mighty night. That is why it has come in the hadith: 'Two nights the like of which creation has not heard of: a night he spends with the dead, not having spent a night with them before; and a night whose morning is the Day of Resurrection.'

flags.arabic: ما حكم اختتان البنات؟ … أن هذا هو الذي يسمى بالخفاض و هو مكرمة … فإذا عرف أهل الخبرة الحاجة إلى ذلك كان مستحبا
flags.context: the first item on this page, in full
options: hold this item from publication pending the Sheikh's office and legal advice
publish only with a prominent preface prepared by the Sheikh's office
publish as an ordinary item in the creed series
flags.note: HIGHEST-PRIORITY EDITORIAL REVIEW (style guide §12). This is the most legally exposed item in the range 521-548. The question is about female circumcision and the answer gives it a ruling. It has been translated exactly as the Sheikh gave it, with nothing softened and nothing strengthened, and every qualifier he attaches has been kept: he calls it a makrumah, a mark of honour; he places it in the recommended (mustaḥabb) category and NOT the obligatory one; he makes even that recommendation conditional on people of expert knowledge recognising a need, and says that where they see no need it is not recommended; and he states expressly that it is not like male circumcision. Removing any of those qualifiers would misrepresent him in one direction, and adding a disclaimer he did not give would misrepresent him in the other. Note for the office: the practice is a criminal offence in the United Kingdom, across the European Union, in Australia and in many other jurisdictions where this English corpus will be read, and publication of a text presenting it as recommended carries real legal and reputational exposure regardless of the qualifiers. The decision whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office, and this item should not ship by default. The answer is also only four lines long and defines nothing about what the procedure is taken to involve.

flags.context: أن هذا هو الذي يسمى بالخفاض و هو مكرمة
options: al-khifāḍ … a mark of honour (makrumah)
female circumcision … an honour
khifāḍ … an ennobling act
flags.note: Both terms are technical. الخفاض is the classical Arabic term used specifically of the female procedure, distinct from الختان used of the male, and the Sheikh preserves that distinction and ends by insisting on it. مكرمة is the term from the report 'circumcision is a sunnah for men, a makrumah for women'; it is a grading term, not a general compliment, and its force is exactly what a reviewing scholar must weigh. The Arabic has been kept beside the English for both. Neither word should be rendered in a way that either elevates the ruling toward the obligatory or lowers it below what he said.

flags.arabic: والإيمان به واجب والسؤال عنه بدعة
flags.context: Malik's reply on the rising over the Throne, in the second item
options: belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation
faith in it is required, and questioning it is a novelty
it must be believed, and enquiring into it is innovation
flags.note: NOTE ON §8. This item is about the divine attributes, which is the context in which the kalām exemption applies — but wājib here attaches to the human act of believing, not to a proposition about God, so it is a genuine obligation and is rendered 'obligatory'. A later reviser must not reclassify it as the modal 'necessarily true'. The famous reply of Malik is given by the Sheikh without a source, and none has been supplied.

flags.arabic: ومن هنا فإن أهل الغلو سواء كان ذلك الغلو في شخص رسول الله (ص) الذي قال …
options: render the broken construction as it stands (done here)
complete the sentence so that it reads grammatically in English
mark the break with an editorial note in the body
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. The sentence beginning 'From here, the people of excess — whether that excess concerns…' never reaches its predicate; the Sheikh breaks off into the hadith and continues from there. This is characteristic of a transcribed spoken answer. The break has been preserved rather than repaired, per style guide §11; completing it would put words in his mouth about what the people of excess are or deserve, in an answer that is precisely about declaring others unbelievers.

flags.arabic: ما رأيكم فيمن يضلل العلماء ويكفرهم لأنهم لا يتغالون في تقديس رسول الله؟
flags.context: the third item as a whole
options: publish with a preface from the Sheikh's office
hold from publication pending the Sheikh's office
publish as an ordinary item in the creed series
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW ADVISED (style guide §12). The answer criticises both excess in venerating the Prophet and laxity, and it takes a position in a dispute that divides communities. Its balance is the whole point, and an excerpt from either half misrepresents it: he rejects the displays of excess AND insists that love of the Prophet above one's own self is a condition of faith. Both halves must travel together.

flags.context: أول ما يلقاه الإنسان في قبره ضمة القبر التي تختلف منها الأضلاع و تزول منها الحمائل
options: and the bearing-straps come apart
and the shoulder-slings are displaced
and the supporting sinews give way
flags.note: حمائل is the plural of حمالة, the strap by which a sword or a load is carried, and it is not the usual word in descriptions of the squeezing of the grave. It may be being used anatomically here, of what holds the frame together. The image has been kept literal rather than resolved into an anatomical term the Arabic does not use.

flags.arabic: وسمع أنه مسح على رأس صبي كان أقرع فنبت شعره
flags.context: the Musaylimah anecdote in the fourth item
options: follow this page's version — the boy was bald and his hair grew
follow the version in article 529 — the boy did not go grey
record both versions
flags.note: SOURCE VARIATION. The Sheikh tells the same anecdote in article 529 of this slice with the detail reversed: there the Prophet wiped the head of a boy who then did not go grey, and Musaylimah's touch left a boy bald. Here the Prophet's touch makes hair grow on a bald boy and Musaylimah's leaves a sound boy bald. Each article has been translated from its own text rather than harmonised.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

Five separate fatwas are published on this one page, divided in the source by rules of hyphens. The rules are preserved in both body_ar and body_en so the boundaries survive; the site should render them as five separate items. Each item's own heading is part of the source text and has been kept. NOTE that the five are of very unequal sensitivity — see the flags — so the page should not be published or withheld as a single unit without that being a deliberate choice.

IMPORTANT: the first item is on female circumcision. It carries the highest-priority editorial flag in this slice and should not be published by default. Every qualifier the Sheikh attaches to his ruling has been preserved in the English.

The ruling words have been carried exactly: مكرمة, استحباب and مستحب in the first item (the recommended category, not the obligatory); واجب of the act of believing in the second; حرم and نهى in the fourth. None has been raised or lowered.

The Sheikh gives no collection and no grading for any of the reports quoted in this file — the hadith of extolling, the bedouin who trembled, the exchange with Umar, the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and Anas, Malik's reply, or the hadith of the two nights. None has been supplied.

In the third item the Sheikh moves from his own voice into the Prophet's and back without marking the transition; the English uses quotation marks to keep the reported words distinguishable, which the Arabic does by context alone.

Source spellings preserved verbatim in body_ar: وتعلى for وتعالى in the second heading, هيآته for هيئاته, ذالك (three times) for ذلك, دعي and لدعى for دعا, رأي for رأى, مالم and لذاك written without spaces or with a dropped letter, and كلما شهد له به where the sense requires ما شهد.
dec: Gives a ruling on female circumcision. The practice is a criminal offence in the United Kingdom, across the EU, in Australia and elsewhere this corpus will be read.
